`hydrofabric` builds hydrologic modeling fabrics from a reference hydrographic
network. Each VPU runs through three phases, **refactor**, **aggregate** and
**nextgen**, and the VPUs are then **merged** into domain products with globally
unique identifiers. The examples need reference data and grids, so they are not
run when this vignette is built.

The terms used here (flowpath, divide, flowline, nexus, hydrolocation, VPU) are
those of the [hydrofabric data model](https://lynker-spatial.github.io/hfdatamodel/).

## Inputs

A build needs a reference GeoPackage (`flowpaths` and `divides`), a
hydrolocation GeoPackage, and flow-direction and flow-accumulation grids;
channel, lake and lake-mask tables are optional. See `vignette("inputs")`. Raw
hydrolocation points are snapped to the reference with
`prepare_hydrolocations()`.

## One VPU

```{r}
library(hydrofabric)

run_pipeline(
  vpuid               = "01",
  reference_gpkg      = "reference.gpkg",
  hydrolocations_gpkg = "hydrolocations.gpkg",
  fdr_path            = "fdr.vrt",
  fac_path            = "fac.vrt",
  out_dir             = "out"
)
```

The product is `out/vpu_01/ngen_vpu01.gpkg`. `from` and `through` run part of the
pipeline:

```{r}
run_pipeline(..., through = "aggregate")   # stop before the nextgen phase
run_pipeline(..., from    = "aggregate")   # resume from a refactored fabric
```

Phase parameters are arguments of each phase function, and `run_pipeline()`
passes them through:

```{r}
run_pipeline(..., min_area_sqkm = 5, coverage_min = 0.95)
```

See the [refactor](refactor.html), [aggregate](aggregate.html),
[nextgen](nextgen.html) and [merge](merge.html) vignettes for each phase.

## All VPUs

`run_vpus()` runs a set of VPUs. Shared inputs are given once, and each domain
overrides only what differs for it:

```{r}
conus <- c("01","02","03N","03S","03W","04","05","06","07","08","09",
           "10L","10U","11","12","13","14","15","16","17","18")

inputs <- stats::setNames(vector("list", length(conus)), conus)
inputs[["19"]] <- list(reference_gpkg = "ak_reference.gpkg",
                       fdr_path = "ak/fdr.vrt", fac_path = "ak/fac.vrt")
inputs[["20"]] <- list(reference_gpkg = "hi_reference.gpkg",
                       fdr_path = "hi/hi_fdr.vrt", fac_path = "hi/hi_fac.vrt")
inputs[["21"]] <- list(reference_gpkg = "prvi_reference.gpkg",
                       fdr_path = "prvi/prvi_fdr.tif", fac_path = "prvi/prvi_fac.tif")

res <- run_vpus(
  inputs,
  out_dir             = "out",
  reference_gpkg      = "conus_reference.gpkg",
  hydrolocations_gpkg = "hydrolocations.gpkg",
  fdr_path            = "conus/fdr.vrt",
  fac_path            = "conus/fac.vrt",
  merge               = TRUE)

subset(res, status != "ok")
```

A failed VPU does not stop the others. `merge = TRUE` merges only when every VPU
succeeded, because the merge assigns one id pool across the whole set.

To merge separately:

```{r}
vpus <- names(inputs)
merge_vpus(
  gpkg_map = as.list(setNames(
    file.path("out", paste0("vpu_", vpus), sprintf("ngen_vpu%s.gpkg", vpus)), vpus)),
  out_dir  = "out/global"
)
```

## Domains

| Domain | VPU | Network | Grids | CRS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SuperCONUS | 01-18 | Lynker Reference Fabric | NHDPlus V2.1 (HydroSHEDS v2 fallback) | EPSG:5070 |
| Alaska | 19 | TDX-Hydro | HydroSHEDS v2 | EPSG:3338 |
| Hawaii | 20 | NHDPlus HR | NHDPlus HR | Hawaii Albers Equal Area Conic |
| PRVI | 21 | NHDPlus HR | NHDPlus HR | EPSG:6566 |
| Guam | 22 | NHDPlus HR | NHDPlus HR | EPSG:32655 |

Guam is supported but not part of the NWM v4 delivery.

## Validation and tests

Every phase checks its output against the invariant suite, and the nextgen phase
stops the build when a gating check fails. See `vignette("invariants")`.

The unit and functional tests, including the acyclic and non-dendritic checks,
run from the installed package and the `tests/` directory:

```r
library(testthat); library(hydrofabric)
test_dir("tests/testthat")
```

## Identifiers

Integer feature ids are Lynker Reference Fabric ids, matched to NHD COMIDs where
a correspondence exists. Columns named `*_comid` carry these ids. The `network`
table traces every reference id through to the flowpath that contains it.
